atalh-y-k.name: Çatalhöyük
atalh-y-k.summary: A very large Neolithic and Chalcolithic proto-city settlement in southern Anatolia that existed from about 7500 to 5600 BCE, notable for its size and apparent egalitarian society.

konya-karaman-plain.name: Konya Plain
konya-karaman-plain.summary: Flat plain at 900–1050 metres in Turkey's Central Anatolia region, forming most of the Konya Basin and the core of the Central Anatolian Plateau.

ay-n.name: Çayönü
ay-n.summary: A Pre-Pottery Neolithic B settlement in southeastern Turkey that flourished from about 8630 to 6800 BC and is an early example of agriculture.

cybele.name: Cybele
cybele.summary: Anatolian mother goddess dating back to earliest Neolithic Çatalhöyük, adopted by the Greeks and later worshipped in Rome as 'Magna Mater', linked to mountains, fertility and wild animals.

urfa-man.name: Urfa Man
urfa-man.summary: A human-shaped stone statue found near Urfa in southeastern Turkey, dated to about 9000 BC and considered the oldest known naturalistic life-sized sculpture of a person.

g-bekli-tepe.name: Göbekli Tepe
g-bekli-tepe.summary: A Neolithic archaeological site in Upper Mesopotamia (modern Turkey), inhabited from about 9500 to at least 8000 BCE, known for huge stone pillars carved with animal and human figures, among the world's oldest megaliths.

pre-pottery-neolithic.name: Pre-Pottery Neolithic
pre-pottery-neolithic.summary: The early Neolithic period in the Near East, roughly 12,000 to 8,500 years ago, marking the early stages of plant and animal domestication before pottery came into use.

mureybet.name: Mureybet
mureybet.summary: An ancient settlement mound on the Euphrates in northern Syria, occupied from about 10,200 to 8000 BC and the type site for the early-farming Mureybetian culture.

beycesultan.name: Beycesultan
beycesultan.summary: Archaeological site in western Anatolia, Turkey, near the modern city of Çivril, along a tributary of the Maeander River.

yumuktepe.name: Yumuktepe
yumuktepe.summary: A tell, or ruin mound, in the city of Mersin, Turkey; once on the town's outskirts, it was later surrounded as the city grew.

nor-untepe.name: Norşuntepe
nor-untepe.summary: An archaeological settlement mound in eastern Turkey occupied from the Chalcolithic to the Iron Age, excavated between 1968 and 1974.

kura-araxes-culture.name: Kura–Araxes culture
kura-araxes-culture.summary: Archaeological culture that existed from about 4000 to 2000 BC across the Caucasus and nearby regions, marked by a sedentary agricultural economy and named after the Kura and Araxes river valleys.

shengavit-site.name: Shengavit
shengavit-site.summary: A Bronze Age archaeological site near Yerevan, Armenia, inhabited from about 3000 to 2500 BCE, and a type site for the Kura-Araxes culture.

maykop-culture.name: Maykop culture
maykop-culture.summary: A Bronze Age archaeological culture (c. 3700-3000 BC) of the western Caucasus, likely ancestral to the Northwest Caucasian language family, named for a royal burial mound in the Kuban River valley.

yamnaya-culture.name: Yamnaya culture
yamnaya-culture.summary: A Copper to early Bronze Age culture of the Pontic–Caspian steppe (3300–2600 BC), known for pit-grave burials under kurgans and often linked to Proto-Indo-European origins.

arslantepe.name: Arslantepe
arslantepe.summary: An ancient city, also known as Melid, on a tributary of the upper Euphrates near modern Malatya, Turkey; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

margahovit.name: Margahovit
margahovit.summary: A village in Armenia's Lori Province, near a site where stone and clay molds for casting weapons of the Kura-Araxes culture were found.

pre-pottery-neolithic-b.name: Pre-Pottery Neolithic B (PPNB)
pre-pottery-neolithic-b.summary: The second stage of the Pre-Pottery Neolithic, centred in upper Mesopotamia and the Levant from about 8,800 to 6,500 BC, developing from the earlier PPNA culture with likely influence from northeastern Anatolia.

ararat-plain.name: Ararat Plain
ararat-plain.summary: One of the largest plains of the Armenian Highlands, split by the Aras River between Armenia and Turkey, bordered by Mount Aragats and Mount Ararat.

colchis.name: Colchis
colchis.summary: An ancient region on the eastern Black Sea coast, now western Georgia, known in Greek mythology as home to the Golden Fleece and Medea and the destination of the Argonauts.

lake-urmia.name: Lake Urmia
lake-urmia.summary: A salt lake in Iranian Azerbaijan that was once one of the world's largest saltwater lakes but has shrunk drastically from drought and damming.

godedzor.name: Godedzor
godedzor.summary: A prehistoric archaeological site in Armenia used seasonally by pastoralists, with its main activity dated between 3650 and 3350 BC.

leyla-tepe-culture.name: Leyla-Tepe Culture
leyla-tepe-culture.summary: A Chalcolithic culture of the South Caucasus, dated to about 3800-3200 BC and named after a site in Azerbaijan, first identified by a Soviet archaeologist in the 1980s.

uruk-period.name: Uruk period
uruk-period.summary: The era, roughly 4000 to 3100 BC, when the first cities and states arose in Mesopotamia, named after the city of Uruk where innovations like the potter's wheel appeared.

tell-hazna.name: Tell Hazna
tell-hazna.summary: An archaeological site in Syria's Khabur river basin, inhabited during the Early Dynastic, Uruk, and Ubaid periods.

uruk.name: Uruk
uruk.summary: An ancient Mesopotamian city that, at its peak around 3100 BC, may have been the largest urban settlement in the world, with tens of thousands of residents.

ubaid-period.name: Ubaid period
ubaid-period.summary: A prehistoric period of Mesopotamia lasting roughly from 6500 to 3800 BC, marking the earliest known settlements on the southern Mesopotamian alluvial plain.

gadachrili-gora.name: Gadachrili Gora
gadachrili-gora.summary: Neolithic archaeological site in Georgia, home to the Shulaveri–Shomu culture, yielding some of the earliest evidence of wheat domestication and winemaking.

shulaveri-shomu-culture.name: Shulaveri–Shomu culture
shulaveri-shomu-culture.summary: A Late Neolithic to Eneolithic archaeological culture found in present-day Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia and parts of northern Iran, lasting from about the 7th to the early 5th millennium BC.

neval-ori.name: Nevalı Çori
neval-ori.summary: An early Neolithic settlement on the middle Euphrates in Turkey, dated to 8400-8100 BC, known for some of the world's oldest temples and monumental sculpture.

a-kl-h-y-k.name: Aşıklı Höyük
a-kl-h-y-k.summary: A Pre-Pottery Neolithic settlement mound in central Turkey, first settled around 8,200 BC, smaller than nearby Çatalhöyük but linked by obsidian trade as far as Cyprus and Iraq.

james-mellaart.name: James Mellaart
james-mellaart.summary: British-Dutch archaeologist (1925–2012) who excavated major prehistoric sites including Çatalhöyük, though later found to have fabricated evidence throughout his career.
